data.about: A page of history: Plate II of Jerome Sondericker’s "Graphic Statics" (MIT, 1903). Half of a symmetrical three-hinged arch carries dead load on its outer chord and wind on the right side. The reactions of the hinges locate the pole P; the funicular polygon of the joint loads drawn through the hinges is the LINE OF PRESSURE, and wherever it leaves the rib, the tension-only diagonals must work — the method of shears and moments picks the active counter of every panel. The Maxwell diagram (the book’s Fig. 3A) then delivers every member force, checked on members 4-5 and 12-14.

steps.caption: a drawing from 1903, brought back to life — step through with the slider, press play, or use ←/→
steps.title: How to draw this scheme

steps.caption: left: the rib spans from the end hinge to the middle hinge at the crown — a vertical end post (5 + 6 + 8.05 ft), an outer chord straight at SLOPE 30°, and an inner chord: a 30-ft-radius arc rising into a straight parallel to the outer chord
steps.title: Half of a three-hinged arch

steps.caption: left: struts perpendicular to the outer chord (the member 7-4 instead bisects the inner arc); every panel gets TWO thin diagonals — tension counters, only one of each pair can work; the spaces are numbered 1–18 in Bow’s notation, as on the plate
steps.title: The web: struts and counters

steps.caption: left: dead load on the outer chord and wind normal to the right slope combine into one inclined load per joint — right: laid tip-to-tail they bend the load line A…I (the dead leg meets the wind leg)
steps.title: Dead load and wind

steps.caption: the three-hinge condition (moments about each end hinge, the leeward rib carries dead load only) fixes the crown force — left: it appears as the green thrust at the middle hinge — right: its components H and V, plotted from I, locate the pole P
steps.title: The middle hinge: H and V

steps.caption: left: a funicular for the two RESULTANTS (dead, wind): string (i) through the crown, string (k) between the resultants, closing string (a) — right: the three rays P–I, P–K, P–A they are drawn parallel to; the closing string lands EXACTLY on the end hinge, so P is right
steps.title: Checking the pole

steps.caption: right: P→I is the reaction at the middle hinge, A→P at the end hinge — left: the same two forces push at the hinges; with the loads they close one polygon P I H G F E D C B A P
steps.title: The reactions of the hinges

steps.caption: left: the funicular polygon of the joint loads, drawn through the hinges (heavy): every string is the line of action of the resultant force on the rib to either side — right: its magnitude is the corresponding ray from P
steps.title: The LINE OF PRESSURE

steps.caption: left: the pressure line decides — method of shears (panel g), of moments (panel c): the WORKING diagonal of every pair is drawn in, its partner stays pale and slack — right: the rays P–G and P–C whose strings carry those resultants
steps.title: Which counters work?

steps.caption: left: the moment arm from the joint 0 square onto the string c (dashed) — right: the ray P–C is that resultant’s magnitude; force × arm ÷ the arm of c-8 gives its stress — the book computes 35 250 lbs compression
steps.title: The stress in c-8 by moments

steps.caption: left: at the middle hinge only TWO members meet the crown load and the reaction PI — right: through H parallel to the outer chord h-18, through P… the polygon closes at the pole 18: both force segments drawn PARALLEL to their members, as the members flash
steps.title: The crown joint closes first

steps.caption: left: the joint under load gh and its inner mate close, their members drawn in — right: chord g-16, the counter and the inner chord 17-p appear PARALLEL to them; poles 17 and 18 COINCIDE, so the strut gh–I₉ carries NOTHING
steps.title: Panel g — joints gh and I₉

steps.caption: left: the next pair of joints closes: chord, strut and counter drawn in — right: chord f-14, the strut 15-16, the counter and the inner chord close on the poles 14 and 15, every segment parallel to its member
steps.title: Panel f — joints fg and I₈

steps.caption: left: the joint under load ef and its inner mate I₇ close — right: poles 12 and 13; the inner chord pieces here carry the LARGEST tension of the whole arch
steps.title: Panel e — joints ef and I₇

steps.caption: left: the joints de and I₆ close — the pressure line crosses the rib right here, which is where the counters change family — right: poles 10 and 11 land far left
steps.title: Panel d — joints de and I₆

steps.caption: left: the joint 0 of the book’s moment method (= I₅) and its outer mate cd close — right: poles 8 and 9; the chord c-8 closes at exactly the force the book computed by moments
steps.title: Panel c — joints cd and 0

steps.caption: left: the joints bc and I₄ close, the last inclined panel — right: poles 6 and 7; the outer chord b-6 approaches its maximum
steps.title: Panel b — joints bc and I₄

steps.caption: left: the joint ab under the biggest tributary and I₃, the foot of the 7-4 strut — right: poles 4 and 5; the counter of the tall panel and the member 7-4 close in one move
steps.title: The tall panel — B₃ and I₃

steps.caption: left: the post joints and both feet flash — right: poles 1, 2, 3 close against the space a, and at the SUPPORT the last polygon shuts on the end reaction AP: the Cremona check
steps.title: Down the end post

steps.caption: blue = compression (outer chord, post, struts), pink = tension (inner chord above the crossing, the working counters); pale = slack counters and the zero strut; pipes ∝ force — drag the sliders: wind off, and the arch calms; click any joint for its equilibrium
steps.title: Compression and tension
